Fern stems rise as columns through cathedral shadow, hard shafts of amber light driving between them to the floor, where one curled crozier has unfurled just enough to cup a single perfect bead of dew that holds the whole canopy inside it.

Fallen log become a mountain range, bark lifting in overhanging shelves crusted with orange bracket fungi stepping up the ridge in tiers, soft green moss padding every ledge, a beetle-bored hole in the underside letting in one bright needle of gold light.

Autumn leaf-litter floor blazing in tangerine and rust, curled leaves arching into tunnels and caves deep enough to walk through, the undersides pale as bone, one leaf-cave entrance framing a corridor of amber shadow stretching back twenty body-lengths into warm dark.

Rain puddle vast as an inland sea, canopy reflected in it with photographic precision, a single drowned ginkgo leaf resting on the bottom in perfect golden silhouette, the surface just trembling where a drop from a fern tip is still falling.

Cycad crown seen from directly beneath, every frond radiating outward like the ribs of a vaulted ceiling, backlit so the leaflets burn electric green along their edges, and at the very centre a new frond coiled tight as a fist, just beginning to open.

Horsetail forest dense at the water's edge, jointed stems banded bright green and grey rising like pillars into the canopy overhead, the whorled collars at each joint catching light like tiny chandeliers, the mud between the stems printed with the press of passing feet.

Root buttress rising as a cliff wall, a natural archway worn under its lowest sweep, the threshold packed with soft liverwort in a dozen shades of green, the passage beyond lit by a single coin of light falling through the canopy onto bare dark soil.

Mushroom ring standing as a full settlement, caps at shoulder height, waist height, knee height, each one tilted to a different angle, the gills beneath catching the light in tight pale rows, one cap holding a pooled raindrop at its exact centre like a mirror.

Moss in full living depth, the surface a landscape of hummocks and valleys, every hummock a different green from chartreuse to almost black, dew caught in the nap like thousands of tiny lanterns, a corridor of lower ground between two ridges running straight into the shade.

A single shaft of white light hits one small patch of bare soil and fern-root in absolute isolation, the rest of the floor lost in blue-green dark, the illuminated patch burning gold, a spiral of seed-fluff resting in it perfectly still as if pinned there.

Fern stems in full colonial density, the columns close enough that the shafts of morning light between them are narrow and precise, each one striking the floor at a different angle, every stem edged in backlit copper where fronds overlap the light path above.

Fallen log so far into rot it has become a slow ridge of rust and ochre fibre, bracket fungi in creamy tiers stepping up the south face, the overhang of each bracket deep enough to stand under, water still dripping from the lowest rim in a slow chain.

Leaf-litter terrain of full deep autumn, the floor stacked two body-lengths deep in places, curled leaves forming enclosed chambers, one large ginkgo fan-leaf bridging a gap between two mounds making a perfect amber roof with the light pressing through it in warm diffusion.

Puddle lake silver and still, the whole araucaria crown above mirrored in it without distortion, a dead horsetail stem lying half-submerged along the near shore, its banded joints showing as green-grey lines through six centimetres of clear water above them.

Cycad crown from beneath in full midday light, fronds forming a perfect radial vault, each leaflet a blade of translucent green where the sun catches it, the oldest fronds at the outer edge brown-tipped and drooping, a spider thread crossing the whole span catching the light across it.

Horsetail stems at flood margin, packed so tightly the gaps between them form a maze of green corridors, each jointed stem throwing a short sharp shadow on the next, the water between the outermost stems perfectly still, holding a broken reflection of the green above.

Root buttress as a great climbing wall, its face seamed with cracks where liverwort has taken hold in long green stripes, the archway at its base worn smooth and dark, a snail track dried to a silver ribbon crossing the threshold and continuing into the dim passage beyond.

Mushroom ring in full morning backlight, each cap rimmed in gold, the gills of the tallest mushroom completely exposed to the low angle, every gill-plate lit separately and casting its own thin shadow, a collapsed cap on the ring's west side already returning to dark slick fibre.

Moss landscape in deep green shade interrupted by one low beam of light striking a single hummock and igniting it from within, the dew-drops on that one hummock burning white while every surrounding surface stays cool and dim, depth of field falling away fast in every direction.

Fern-stem cathedral at dawn, the light coming in nearly horizontal, shafts running the full length of the floor between the columns and striking the far fronds with sideways gold, the floor between the stems covered in a thin mist lying ankle-height, perfectly level, glowing where the shafts cross it.

Deep ginkgo-leaf litter, the fans overlapping in gold and pale yellow, some still holding their lobed shape and others crumbling at the tips, one intact leaf tent-pitched on two rolled neighbours making a low cave, a groove of trapped rainwater running along its central fold still bright.

Mossy log-top ridge, the moss so saturated it is almost turquoise, individual moss-stems visible at this scale as tiny trees, a line of bracket fungi along the log's spine serving as a staircase, the space beneath the lowest bracket a dry amber-lit alcove in the damp green world.

Puddle lake at the foot of a cycad, perfectly still after the rain, the cycad's crown reflected in it radiating outward from the centre so the water looks like a second crown, a single cycad leaflet floating on the surface and casting a long thin shadow across the reflection.

Horsetail edge-forest in afternoon side-light, the banded stems casting horizontal shadows across each other in layered stripes, the far stems almost lost in green shade, the nearest ones lit in full saturated green with the joint-collars catching the light as bright rings at regular intervals up each stem.

A hard shaft of late light driving between two fern columns strikes a patch of moss and lights a spiral of seed-fluff resting there in absolute detail, every fibre of the fluff separately visible, the shadow of the spiral stretching long and dark across the illuminated moss to one side.
